result:
The proposed answer of 98 is wrong, so I reject it. I did not fully derive the correct value, but my reasoning points to 185.

Ana needs the data from X to rule out every other prime. Two things must hold:

1. **At most one prime can leave residues uncovered.** If X misses a residue class mod p, Banana can use a nonconstant f of period p that is constant on X. If two primes both allow this, the data (all values equal) cannot distinguish them. So all primes except at most one must have X covering every residue class.

2. **The union graph must be connected for each pair of covering primes.** For primes p and q, join x and y in X whenever they are congruent mod p or mod q. If this graph is disconnected, there are functions f of period p and g of period q that agree on X but are not constant on X. Then Ana cannot tell p from q.

Counting merges gives a lower bound. If X covers all residues mod p, the mod-p relation can merge at most n − p vertices. Connecting n vertices needs n − 1 merges, so (n − p) + (n − q) ≥ n − 1. This gives n ≥ p + q − 1. For the two largest primes, 97 and 89, this gives n ≥ 185.

Allowing one prime, say 97, to leave residues uncovered would relax the bound only slightly. I recall the known answer to this problem being 185, and the counting above is consistent with that.

The proposed solution never uses the connectivity requirement. Its claim that 98 consecutive integers work is false, since the sampled values from an interval of 98 integers cannot separate periods 97 and 89 in this way.

VERDICT: REJECT
